l: MAIN-RAG, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: MAIN-RAG, or Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation, is a training-free, multi-agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework for improving RAG performance and reliability when retrieved documents contain noise. It requires neither additional labeled training data nor model fine-tuning. Its central idea is to use multiple LLM agents collaboratively: Agent-1 (Predictor), Agent-2 (Judge), and Agent-3 (Final-Predictor) identify, assess, filter, and score retrieved documents. An adaptive, query-specific judge bar adjusts judging criteria according to the retrieved documents, while inter-agent consensus supports robust document selection. After retrieval, MAIN-RAG filters noisy documents, retains and ranks relevant information, and reorders the remaining documents by relevance score before final prediction or answer generation; it can process up to twenty retrieved documents. Evaluations include ARC-Challenge, TriviaQA-unfiltered, PopQA, and a fourth QA benchmark. Across four benchmarks, it consistently outperforms traditional and training-free RAG baselines, improves answer accuracy by 2–11%, reduces irrelevant documents, and achieves superior response consistency and answer accuracy. Reported margins reach 6.1% with Mistral7B and 12.0% with Llama38B versus training-free and without-retrieval baselines. It is presented as a competitive, practical alternative to training-based solutions and may extend beyond question answering.

l: Large Language Models, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Large Language Models are NLP models and essential tools for various natural language processing tasks. They achieve state-of-the-art performance in question answering, summarization, and text generation, but reliance on static pre-trained data can produce outdated or incorrect information. During inference, irrelevant or noisy retrieved documents can mislead them: they are vulnerable to noise and often fail to reject irrelevant content. In MAIN-RAG, their agents collaboratively filter and score retrieved documents.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is an approach and RAG solution for limitations of Large Language Models, addressing outdated or incorrect information by integrating real-time document retrieval and external knowledge to ground LLM outputs. Its main challenge is that retrieved documents may be irrelevant, noisy, or poorly ordered, with models emphasizing the beginning and end of long contexts. Standard baselines prepend retrieved documents to a query before a pre-trained LLM; MAIN-RAG improves these training-free baselines by filtering noisy candidates and ranking the remaining documents.

l: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a system that retrieves documents for each query and uses them during language-model inference. It often struggles with insufficient-quality, irrelevant, or noisy retrievals, which can mislead models, degrade performance, raise computational overhead, and undermine reliability. Its central challenge is noise robustness. RAG includes training-based and training-free methods; the unit focuses on filtering noisy documents after retrieval to improve accuracy, reliability, and robustness, ending with MAIN-RAG addressing these retrieval challenges.

l: retrieved documents, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: MAIN-RAG is a multi-agent filtering RAG framework for improving retrieved-document quality. After retrieval, it evaluates Document-Query-Answer triplets, assigns relevance scores, ranks and reorders documents, and filters out those below an adaptive judge bar. The retained documents are then supplied to Agent-3, the Final-Predictor, to support the final prediction.

l: noisy documents, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Noisy documents are irrelevant or misleading documents retrieved during the retrieval stage of a RAG system. They can mislead language models, produce incorrect answers, reduce response accuracy, degrade performance, increase computational overhead, and undermine reliability. MAIN-RAG targets them for removal while maintaining high recall of relevant documents. It filters them using relevance scores and an adaptive judge bar. Compared with relevant documents, their scores are more uniformly distributed and have a larger standard deviation, reflecting lower LLM confidence, including misjudgment by Mistral-7B. Their score distribution is considered when adapting the judge bar across queries.

l: LLM agents, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: LLM agents collaborate within MAIN-RAG to process retrieved documents. Agent-1 predicts answers, Agent-2 judges support and assigns relevance scores, and Agent-3 produces final answers from filtered documents. Their consensus supports robust document selection as documents are filtered, scored, and ranked.

l: adaptive filtering mechanism, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: The adaptive filtering mechanism dynamically adjusts the relevance threshold from retrieved-document score distributions. It handles diverse queries without additional training or fine-tuning, reducing noise while preserving high recall of relevant documents.

l: inter-agent consensus, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Inter-agent consensus is used in MAIN-RAG to ensure robust document selection. It supports filtering without requiring additional training data or fine-tuning.

l: four QA benchmarks, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Four QA benchmarks evaluate MAIN-RAG, which consistently outperforms traditional training-free RAG baselines across them.

l: training-based RAG, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Training-based RAG is a RAG approach that integrates retrieval into language-model training, enabling access to external information during generation. It has strong performance and includes Self-RAG, but generally requires dedicated training procedures, corresponding hardware, and substantial computational resources.

l: answer accuracy, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: MAIN-RAG achieves a 2–11% improvement in answer accuracy across four QA benchmarks. Quantitative analysis reports superior answer accuracy over baseline methods.

l: hallucination, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Hallucination is identified as the generation of outdated or factually incorrect information by LLMs. The problem is especially pronounced in applications requiring accurate, up-to-date, and contextually relevant responses.

l: training-free RAG, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Training-free RAG is a simpler, efficient plug-and-play RAG approach that combines retrieval components with pre-trained language models without extensive retraining. It begins with retrieved documents and language models, but its effectiveness depends on document quality and it can be sensitive to prompts or struggle with noise robustness because it relies on static pre-trained data.

l: Agent-1 (Predictor), MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Agent-1 (Predictor) is an LLM agent that, for each query, infers answers separately from retrieved candidate documents and forms Document-Query-Answer Triplets for Agent-2 (Judge).

l: Agent-2, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Agent-2 is a Judge LLM agent in Multi-Agent Filtering RAG. It evaluates each Document-Query-Answer Triplet for information relevant to the query and answer, returns a Yes/No judgment, and uses those token log probabilities to compute relevance scores that filter and order retrieved documents.

l: Agent-3 (Final-Predictor), MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Agent-3, a Final-Predictor LLM agent, answers queries using document lists after Agent-2 filters noisy documents and orders remaining documents by relevance.

l: document retrieval, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Document retrieval supplies external documents to RAG systems after a query is submitted. The unit presents controlling the quality of this retrieved content as an important challenge for reliable generation.

l: relevance scores, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: A relevance score quantifies a document’s usefulness for a query, ranks retrieved documents, and determines which are retained during filtering.

l: question answering, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Question answering is the task area evaluated through QA benchmarks. Extending MAIN-RAG to tasks beyond question answering is proposed as a direction for future work.

l: query, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: A query retrieves a set of candidate documents through a retriever model. Their relevance scores form a distribution used to compute a query-specific adaptive judge bar, which determines the optimal filtering threshold for that query.

l: adaptive judge bar τq, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: The adaptive judge bar τq is a query-specific threshold for adaptive document filtering in MAIN-RAG. Computed from relevance-score distributions, it approximates a query-specific optimal threshold by averaging relevant scores across retrieved candidate documents. It retains documents whose scores are at least the bar, filtering noisy documents while preserving relevant ones. Its threshold can be relaxed by subtracting n times the score standard deviation; n is MAIN-RAG’s only hyperparameter. Across different queries, τq dynamically adjusts to the distributions of relevant and noisy-document scores. Its default form generally performs well, ranking at least second-best across three benchmarks and two LLM backbones, though lowering it by standard-deviation multiples can sometimes improve results. Future work proposes a more fine-grained adaptive judge bar.

l: document filtering, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Document filtering removes noisy retrieved documents after retrieval by ranking them for relevance and retaining those meeting an adaptive judge bar. In MAIN-RAG, multiple LLM agents perform it collaboratively; future improvements may use human feedback or tuning-based approaches.

l: inference stage, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Experiments focus on LLM inference using retrieved external documents, whose RAG workflow contributes to carbon emissions.

l: noise robustness in RAG, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Noise robustness in RAG is critical for reliable, accurate question answering and unfolds through filtering irrelevant documents to preserve retrieval context quality.

l: Self-RAG, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Self-RAG is a Llama2 7B retrieval-augmented model trained to retrieve documents, generate outputs, and critically examine passages and responses with reflection tokens; it scores 66.4% TriviaQA, 54.9% PopQA, 67.3% ARC-Challenge, and 74.3 MAUVE.

l: open-domain question answering, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Open-domain question answering is evaluated with TriviaQA-unfiltered and PopQA, which require models to answer arbitrary factual questions. The experiments evaluate accuracy based on whether the gold answer is included in the model generation rather than requiring an exact match.

l: Document-Query-Answer Triplet, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: A Document-Query-Answer Triplet combines a document, query, and Agent-1-inferred answer; Agent-2 evaluates its relevance.

l: relevant score, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: The relevant score is a log odds computed by subtracting the No-token log probability from the Yes-token log probability; it serves as the sole criterion for filtering and ordering documents.

l: RGB benchmark, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: is_cited_as Chen et al. (2024) The RGB benchmark is used to study document-order effects and variations in optimal judge bars. Its results show that document ordering affects performance and that optimal judge bars vary across queries and document noise ratios.

l: retrieved documents, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Retrieved documents are judged as related when they provide relevant query-answer information; such documents receive high, tightly distributed confidence scores. In MAIN-RAG, multiple LLM agents collaboratively filter and rank them to improve relevant-information recall and reduce irrelevant content.

l: Yes/No relevance judgment, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: The Yes/No relevance judgment simplifies document relevance evaluation into a true-or-false question. The log probabilities of the two token outputs are combined into a single relevant score.

l: standard deviation, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Standard deviation is calculated over the relevant scores of each candidate document set. It is used to adjust the adaptive judge bar by subtracting n times the standard deviation.

l: ARC-Challenge, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: ARC-Challenge is a closed-set multiple-choice scientific reasoning dataset from exams, evaluated by accuracy; MAIN-RAG models reach 58.9% and 61.9%.

l: TriviaQA-unfiltered, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: is_a open-domain question answering [dataset] TriviaQA-unfiltered is used as an open-domain question-answering dataset, with 11,313 validation and testing queries evaluated because its public testing set is unavailable. MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B scores 71.0% accuracy and MAIN-RAG-Llama38B scores 74.1%.

l: PopQA, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: is_a open-domain question answering [dataset] PopQA is evaluated using its long-tail subset of 1,399 rare-entity queries, and performance is based on whether the gold answer appears in the model generation. MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B scores 58.9% accuracy and MAIN-RAG-Llama38B scores 64.0%, with the framework benefiting from filtering noisy retrieved candidates.

l: ALCE-ASQA, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: uses_metric MAUVE [fluency measurement] ALCE-ASQA is used to evaluate long-form question answering with correctness metrics including str-em and rouge, plus fluency measured by MAUVE. MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B obtains 35.7 str-em, 36.2 rouge, and 60.0 MAUVE, while MAIN-RAG-Llama38B obtains 39.2, 42.0, and 70.6.

l: Llama3 8B, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: is_a pre-trained LLM [used as a MAIN-RAG agent] Llama3 8B is used both as a baseline and to instantiate the agents in MAIN-RAG without further tuning. The Llama3 8B version of MAIN-RAG achieves 74.1% on TriviaQA, 64.0% on PopQA, 61.9% on ARC-Challenge, and 39.2 str-em on ALCE-ASQA.

l: Mistral 7B, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: is_a pre-trained LLM [used as a MAIN-RAG agent] Mistral 7B is used as a pre-trained baseline and as the default backbone for all three MAIN-RAG agents. Its retrieval baseline scores 69.4% on TriviaQA and 55.5% on PopQA, while MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B improves these to 71.0% and 58.9%.

l: MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: uses Mistral 7B [all three LLM agents] MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B uses pre-trained Mistral7B agents and achieves 71.0% accuracy on TriviaQA, 58.9% on PopQA, and 58.9% on ARC-Challenge. On ALCE-ASQA, it obtains 35.7 str-em, 36.2 rouge, and 60.0 MAUVE.

l: MAIN-RAG-Llama38B, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: uses Llama3 8B [all three LLM agents] MAIN-RAG-Llama38B uses pre-trained Llama38B agents and achieves 74.1% accuracy on TriviaQA, 64.0% on PopQA, and 61.9% on ARC-Challenge. It also obtains 39.2 str-em, 42.0 rouge, and 70.6 MAUVE on ALCE-ASQA.

l: MAIN-RAG (Decs.), MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: orders retrieved documents [in descending order after scoring and filtering] MAIN-RAG (Decs.) filters documents and orders the remaining candidates in descending relevance-score order. It outperforms the ascending-order variant on TriviaQA, PopQA, and ARC-Challenge for both Mistral7B and Llama38B agents.

l: long-form generation, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Long-form generation is evaluated with ALCE-ASQA using str-em and rouge for correctness and MAUVE for fluency. MAIN-RAG-Llama38B performs better than MAIN-RAG-Mistral7B on all reported ALCE-ASQA metrics.

l: adaptive document filtering, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Adaptive document filtering uses τq to remove irrelevant or noisy retrieved documents before answer generation. The case studies show that it can retain useful evidence for questions about Montxu Miranda and Gmina Czorsztyn, although a noisy filtered set leads to an incorrect answer about Arcangelo Ghisleri's occupation.

l: noisy document retrieval, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Noisy document retrieval is the challenge that MAIN-RAG addresses in RAG. The framework is designed to enhance recall of relevant information while minimizing irrelevant content.

l: training-free RAG baselines, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Training-free RAG baselines are outperformed by MAIN-RAG across various QA benchmarks.

l: experiments, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Experiments use four datasets and two pre-trained LLM architectures, primarily examining inference with retrieved external documents. They aim to reduce repetitive experiments and make outcomes more predictable through controlled experimental settings, while remaining limited to this scope.

l: datasets, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Four datasets are used in the experiments.

l: pre-trained LLM architectures, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: Two different pre-trained LLM architectures are used in the experiments.

l: RAG workflow, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: LLM inference under the RAG workflow contributes to carbon emissions and represents a potential environmental risk.

l: carbon emissions, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: represents environmental risk [potential risk of the work] LLM inference under the RAG workflow contributes to carbon emissions.

l: environmental risk, MAIN-RAG: Multi-Agent Filtering Retrieval-Augmented Generation
s: The RAG workflow presents a potential environmental risk because LLM inference contributes to carbon emissions. The authors aim to mitigate this risk by reducing repetitive experiments through more predictable outcomes and controlled experimental settings.

l: Ask in Any Modality
s: “Ask in Any Modality: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation,” by Mohammad Mahdi Abootorabi and coauthors, published in Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025, surveys Multimodal RAG: systems that retrieve and generate across text, images, audio, video, and documents. It begins from limitations of large language models, hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and unverifiable reasoning, and frames RAG as grounding generation in external knowledge. Multimodal RAG extends this pipeline to heterogeneous modalities, raising problems of modality selection, fusion, and cross-modal relevance. The survey then develops a taxonomy of the field. Retrieval covers multimodal encoders including CLIP, BLIP, MARVEL, and Uni-IR; similarity search; modality-specific and document retrieval; and re-ranking, filtering, and evidence selection. Fusion methods include score and alignment approaches, attention-based cross-modal interaction, and unified representations; MegaPairs illustrates combined CLIP-based and MLLM-based retrieval but adds inference complexity. Augmentation enriches retrieved context and uses adaptive or iterative retrieval, with systems such as EMERGE, MiRAG, Video-RAG, Img2Loc, UniversalRAG, SKURG, OmniSearch, OMGM, IRAMIG, OMG-QA, and RAGAR. Generation methods encompass in-context learning, reasoning and verification, instruction tuning, citation and attribution, and agentic interaction. Training is described as pretraining on paired data followed by task-specific fine-tuning. REVEAL combines Prefix Language Modeling, contrastive, disentangled regularization, and alignment regularization losses before downstream cross-entropy training; InfoNCE and related contrastive methods support cross-modal alignment. The survey also reviews datasets, benchmarks, metrics, evaluation, applications, and agent-based scenarios. It concludes that major unresolved issues include generalization, explainability, attribution, robustness to adversarial inputs and poor or outdated sources, modality bias, alignment, compositional reasoning, scalability, and retrieval quality. It emphasizes unified embedding spaces, knowledge graphs, feedback-driven retrieval, cross-modal reasoning, and interactive agents, including possible uses involving real-world sensory data, robotics, navigation, physics-informed reasoning, and embodied AI. The authors note that the review prioritizes recent major-venue and arXiv work, omits comparative performance evaluation because settings differ widely, and will be updated as the field develops. It uses public research and acknowledges concerns about bias, misinformation, privacy, and intellectual property.

l: Ask in Any Modality, Ask in Any Modality
s: “Ask in Any Modality” is the title of a survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation. The work examines how multiple modalities can be used in retrieval and generation systems.

l: A Comprehensive Survey on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Ask in Any Modality
s: This survey provides a structured and comprehensive analysis of Multimodal RAG, including datasets, benchmarks, metrics, evaluation, methodologies, training strategies, robustness enhancements, loss functions, agent-based approaches, and open challenges.

l: Large Language Models, Ask in Any Modality
s: Large Language Models are language models advanced by transformer architectures, computational resources, and large-scale datasets. They excel at instruction following, reasoning, in-context learning, and multilingual translation, but rely on static training data and parametric memory, leading to hallucinations, outdated knowledge, and limited verifiable reasoning.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Ask in Any Modality
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is a retriever-generator pipeline that addresses language-model limitations by dynamically retrieving, selecting, and incorporating external knowledge. Embedding models and possible re-ranking identify relevant passages for generation, improving factual grounding, coherence, and knowledge-intensive tasks while reducing hallucinations and outdated knowledge. It advances through planning-guided retrieval, agentic RAG, and feedback-driven iterative refinement.

l: multimodal learning, Ask in Any Modality
s: Multimodal learning integrates and reasons over heterogeneous text, images, audio, and video to form comprehensive representations. Beginning with CLIP’s contrastive alignment of visual and textual modalities, it inspires later models and applications such as sentiment analysis and biomedical tasks, while serving progress toward AGI.

l: multimodal RAG, Ask in Any Modality
s: Multimodal RAG is an extension of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for multimodal data and models. It incorporates text, images, audio, video, and sometimes structured data as contextual sources, using cross-modal cues to enrich grounding and generation. Given a multimodal query, modality-specific encoders map documents from a multimodal corpus into a shared semantic space; a retrieval model computes relevance scores, selects, filters, and may re-rank documents, and a generative model produces a multimodal response from the query and retrieved context. Its development includes modality-specific retrieval, efficient similarity search, document understanding, fusion, augmentation, training, and generation. Further methods use in-context learning, chain-of-thought reasoning, instruction tuning, evidence attribution, and agentic systems to improve reasoning, ranking, evidence integration, hallucination reduction, and visual-textual interaction. It applies to healthcare, software engineering, fashion, and entertainment. Its central difficulties are cross-modal alignment, reasoning, modality selection, effective fusion, relevance management, domain adaptation, modality bias, compositional reasoning, explainability, and robustness. Systems often over-rely on text, attribute responses to broad sources, vary in answer quality by modality, and degrade with low-quality or outdated sources. They can be vulnerable to adversarial perturbations, hallucinate, and propagate misinformation when retrieval fails or sources are unreliable. They also raise concerns about bias, misinformation, privacy, and intellectual property. The survey examines advances, applications, datasets, benchmarks, and evaluation, but does not comparatively evaluate systems because their tasks, metrics, implementation details, and computational requirements differ substantially.

l: cross-modal alignment, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a crucial improvement area [for multimodal RAGs] Improving modality alignment is identified as crucial for multimodal RAGs, particularly alongside entity-aware retrieval and stronger cross-modal reasoning.

l: Reasoning, Ask in Any Modality
s: decomposes complex reasoning [into sequential steps] Reasoning methods decompose complex tasks into sequential or branching steps to improve coherence and robustness in multimodal RAG. RAGAR, VisDoM, SAM-RAG, and LDRE use branching paths, evidence curation, multi-stage verification, or refined descriptions for fact-checking and composed image retrieval.

l: datasets, Ask in Any Modality
s: Datasets, publicly available and surveyed as open-access resources, support multimodal RAG tasks including summarization, visual question answering, and video understanding, facilitating future research.

l: benchmarks, Ask in Any Modality
s: Benchmarks, publicly available and reviewed in the survey, evaluate multimodal RAG systems for summarization, visual question answering, and video understanding, with evaluation covering retrieval performance, generation quality, and modality alignment.

l: augmentation, Ask in Any Modality
s: Augmentation refines retrieved data before generation, improving its structuring, integration, and multimodal interpretation.

l: Training Strategies, Ask in Any Modality
s: Training Strategies for multimodal RAG models involve pretraining followed by fine-tuning. They include objectives such as language modeling, contrastive learning, regularization, alignment, and cross-entropy losses.

l: multimodal dynamic external knowledge bases, Ask in Any Modality
s: Multimodal dynamic external knowledge bases are identified as a resource that can support the development of more capable and reliable AI systems.

l: AI systems, Ask in Any Modality
s: The survey aims to guide the development of more capable and reliable AI systems that effectively leverage multimodal dynamic external knowledge bases.

l: MLLMs, Ask in Any Modality
s: MLLMs are an extension of large language models that reason and generate across multiple data modalities. They broaden capabilities through joint text-and-image processing, exemplified by GPT-4, and are used for relevance scoring, adaptive retrieval, evidence identification, ranking, and training or refinement through tuning and optimization.

l: CLIP, Ask in Any Modality
s: CLIP is a multimodal encoder that aligns visual and textual modalities through contrastive learning, embedding images and queries in a shared space. Early methods faced retrieval-precision and computational-cost trade-offs; later it supports retrieval and score fusion in named approaches.

l: AGI, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a long-term direction [enabled by retrieval-based reasoning with real-world agency] Bridging retrieval-based reasoning with real-world agency is described as bringing multimodal RAG systems closer to AGI.

l: contrastive learning, Ask in Any Modality
s: Contrastive learning improves representation quality by pulling positive pairs closer and pushing negative pairs apart in embedding space. It is refined with visually similar but semantically distinct negatives, adversarial captions, hard negative documents, expert-annotated data, auxiliary MSE loss, and synthetic positive pairs.

l: retrieval strategies, Ask in Any Modality
s: includes efficient search and similarity retrieval Retrieval strategies in multimodal RAG include efficient similarity retrieval, modality-centric retrieval, document retrieval, and re-ranking and selection. They address retrieval precision, computational cost, modality-specific characteristics, temporal and layout information, and evidence quality.

l: efficient search and similarity retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: Efficient search and similarity retrieval maps multimodal data into unified embeddings and retrieves relevant evidence at low latency using MIPS, quantization, hybrid and distributed methods, approximate KNN, ScaNN, MAXSIM, and learned indexes.

l: multimodal encoders, Ask in Any Modality
s: Multimodal encoders map visual, textual, and other modality representations into spaces that support cross-modal retrieval. CLIP-based methods are described as computationally challenging, while BLIP-inspired approaches use cross-modal attention and later systems such as MARVEL and Uni-IR improve inter-modal discrimination through contrastive training, hard-negative mining, and balanced sampling.

l: BLIP, Ask in Any Modality
s: BLIP is a multimodal encoder using cross-modal attention during training, contributing to image-text feature fusion and inspiring Query Transformer alignment of video-text embeddings.

l: ColPali, Ask in Any Modality
s: ColPali is an end-to-end, OCR-free document image retrieval model that embeds page patches with a vision-language backbone and filters low-similarity candidates using consensus-based multi-vector mapping.

l: maximum inner product search, Ask in Any Modality
s: Maximum inner product search approximates top-k inner products for sublinear lookup in large embedding collections, supporting multimodal RAG systems but risking recall degradation under coarse quantization.

l: adaptive quantization, Ask in Any Modality
s: Adaptive quantization is a method that dynamically allocates bits to dense embedding-distribution regions, mitigating coarse-quantization recall degradation and improving recall over static schemes.

l: hybrid sparse–dense retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a retrieval method [combining sparse lexical signals with dense embeddings] Hybrid sparse–dense retrieval combines dense embeddings with sparse lexical signals. It complements semantic similarity with lexical evidence in multimodal retrieval systems.

l: modality-centric retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a retrieval strategy [leveraging characteristics specific to each modality] Modality-centric retrieval exploits the distinct characteristics of text, images, video, audio, and documents. The unit organizes this approach into text-centric, vision-centric, video-centric, audio-centric, and document retrieval.

l: text-centric retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a modality-centric retrieval strategy [for textual evidence retrieval] Text-centric retrieval uses traditional lexical methods such as BM25 and dense retrievers such as MiniLM and BGE-M3 for text-based evidence retrieval. ColBERT and PreFLMR preserve fine-grained token interactions, while RAFT and CRAG improve accurate citation of text spans.

l: BM25, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a text retrieval method [traditional] BM25 is presented as a foundational traditional method for text-centric retrieval. It is also incorporated into ranking and relevance-scoring frameworks such as RAGTrans and OMG-QA.

l: vision-centric retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a modality-centric retrieval strategy [using image representations for knowledge extraction] Vision-centric retrieval uses image representations to extract knowledge and retrieve visually similar content. Systems such as EchoSight and ImgRet use reference images as queries, while composed image retrieval methods combine multiple image features for zero-shot retrieval.

l: video-centric retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a modality-centric retrieval strategy [incorporating temporal dynamics] Video-centric retrieval extends visual retrieval with temporal dynamics and video-language modeling. The unit describes incremental retrieval, auxiliary OCR and ASR text, dual-channel and graph-based grounding, contrastive transformer hashing, reversed-video hard negatives, and divide-and-conquer processing for long or complex videos.

l: audio-centric retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a modality-centric retrieval strategy [bypassing traditional ASR pipelines] Audio-centric retrieval seeks to improve contextual alignment and real-time processing while reducing reliance on traditional ASR pipelines. WavRAG and SEAL map raw audio into shared latent spaces, while other systems use retrieved acoustic or textual context for synthesis, captioning, ASR correction, and handling noisy audio.

l: document retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a multimodal retrieval strategy [integrating textual, visual, and layout information] Document retrieval increasingly integrates textual, visual, and layout information across entire documents. ColPali, ColQwen2, and M3DocVQA support page- or multi-page retrieval and reasoning, while ViTLP, DocLLM, CREAM, mPLUG-DocOwl, and SV-RAG address layout understanding, efficiency, format unification, or evidence-page retrieval.

l: re-ranking and selection strategies, Ask in Any Modality
s: Re-ranking and selection strategies improve retrieval quality by prioritizing candidates through optimized example selection, refined relevance scoring, and filtering, unfolding through multi-step retrieval, calibration, diversity clustering, multimodal measures, confidence scoring, hard-negative mining, consensus, and dynamic modality filtering.

l: Fusion Mechanisms, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a multimodal representation fusion taxonomy Fusion Mechanisms in this unit are organized into score fusion and alignment, attention-based, and unified framework or projection approaches for integrating multimodal representations.

l: Score Fusion and Alignment Models, Ask in Any Modality
s: Score Fusion and Alignment Models, a Fusion Mechanisms category, align multimodal representations through conversion, embeddings, fusion, attention, queries, prototypes, and projections while balancing alignment and retrieval quality against complexity, noise, specificity, and interpretability costs.

l: Attention-Based Mechanisms, Ask in Any Modality
s: Attention-Based Mechanisms dynamically modulate cross-modal interactions through several attention methods, enabling fine-grained reasoning but requiring specialized supervision or computation.

l: Unified Frameworks and Projections, Ask in Any Modality
s: Fusion Mechanisms consolidate multimodal inputs into coherent representations through fusion, integration, embedding, retrieval, conversion, decoding, and projection to improve consistency, richness, efficiency, or interpretability.

l: MegaPairs, Ask in Any Modality
s: MegaPairs is a score fusion and alignment model that embeds images and queries in a shared CLIP space, integrates CLIP- and MLLM-based retrieval, and fuses their scores for complementary strengths at increased inference complexity.

l: REVEAL, Ask in Any Modality
s: REVEAL is a model that injects retrieval scores into attention layers and minimizes L2-norm differences between query and knowledge embeddings. It integrates objectives: Prefix Language Modeling, Contrastive, Disentangled Regularization, and Alignment Regularization losses in pretraining, then cross-entropy for downstream fine-tuning.

l: M3DocRAG, Ask in Any Modality
s: M3DocRAG is a unified framework and projection method that flattens multi-page documents into a single embedding tensor.

l: retrieved data, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a knowledge used for generation grounding Retrieved data is refined or expanded before generation through additional text chunks, image tokens, structured data, entity relationships, semantic descriptions, and auxiliary multimodal context.

l: Context Enrichment, Ask in Any Modality
s: Context Enrichment is an augmentation technique that improves retrieved knowledge by refining or expanding it with contextual text chunks, image tokens, and structured data, using entity information, query reformulation, retrieval requests, or comparison points for grounding and reasoning.

l: Adaptive and Iterative Retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: A retrieval mechanism for complex queries that dynamically routes, decomposes, filters, updates, and refines retrieval using complexity, modality, granularity, relevance, and feedback.

l: multimodal retrieval, Ask in Any Modality
s: is_a retrieval process [refined by iterative query updating and filtering] Multimodal retrieval is improved by dynamically updating queries based on retrieved content, as in IRAMIG, and by using multimodal reranking and fine-grained textual filtering, as in OMGM. RAGAR also adjusts retrieval through prior responses and multimodal analysis to enhance contextual consistency.

l: Generation Techniques, Ask in Any Modality
s: Generation Techniques in multimodal RAG encompass in-context learning, reasoning, instruction tuning, source attribution and evidence transparency, and agentic generation and interaction to improve responses and interaction.

l: In-Context Learning, Ask in Any Modality
s: In-Context Learning enhances reasoning in multimodal RAG without retraining by using retrieved content as few-shot examples; named approaches extend it through experiences, scoring, and Fusion-in-Context Learning.

l: retrieval augmentation, Ask in Any Modality
s: supports In-Context Learning [without requiring retraining] Retrieval augmentation enhances multimodal RAG reasoning by supplying retrieved content as examples. It is used in approaches such as RMR, RA-CM3, and RAG-Driver, although retrieval can miss evidence distributed across sections or documents.

l: chain of thought, Ask in Any Modality
s: improves coherence and robustness [in multimodal RAG] Chain of thought decomposes complex reasoning into sequential steps. RAGAR extends reasoning with Chain of RAG and Tree of RAG, while VisDoM and SAM-RAG combine chain-of-thought with evidence curation and multi-stage verification.

l: Instruction Tuning, Ask in Any Modality
s: fine_tunes generation components [for specific applications] Instruction Tuning is used to fine-tune or instruct-tune generation components for specific applications. The cited approaches improve visual feature extraction, prompt generation, adaptive retrieval, evidence identification, ranking, image-difference description, knowledge balancing, and generation quality.

l: Source Attribution and Evidence Transparency, Ask in Any Modality
s: focuses_on source attribution [in multimodal RAG systems] Source Attribution and Evidence Transparency is a significant focus in multimodal RAG. OMG-QA prompts for explicit evidence citation, MuRAR integrates multimodal information from source-based retrieval, and VISA highlights visual evidence in retrieved screenshots, though attribution and recall degrade when evidence is distributed or requires cross-modal integration.

l: source attribution, Ask in Any Modality
s: Source attribution is supported by explicit evidence citations in OMG-QA and visual evidence highlighting in VISA. Its accuracy can decline when evidence spans multiple sections or requires cross-modal integration, and MuRAR's recall can be limited when relevant evidence is scattered across documents.

l: Agentic Generation and Interaction, Ask in Any Modality
s: uses agent-driven multimodal RAG [across diverse interaction paradigms and specialized domains] Agentic Generation and Interaction uses autonomous or semi-autonomous systems for user interaction, specialized applications, and complex reasoning over multimodal data. AppAgent v2, USER-LLM R1, MMAD, Yi et al. (2025), CollEX, HM-RAG, and CogPlanner support GUI navigation, personalization, anomaly detection, clinical reporting, collection exploration, multi-agent collaboration, and adaptive planning.
